rv.q: If Pasadena Playhouse is aiming to reinvent landmark American musicals for contemporary audiences, their production of Brigadoon is an absolute triumph.
In an era that can feel equally uncertain, Brigadoon still offers that escape, inviting audiences to believe, if only for an evening, in the impossible.
Pasadena Playhouse has done just that and come up with something quite spectacular indeed.
The miracle of this production is that someone in Pasadena remembered how to wake it up.
Yet this adaptation of a play not seen on Broadway since 1980 makes suspension of disbelief remarkably easy.
Highlights of this production include an updated script by Alexandra Silber, a glorious ensemble of performers and dancers and sensational direction and choreography by Katie Spelman.
Beautifully performed by Keller, it’s a transformative scene that, among Silber’s other innovations, burnishes the rusty Brigadoon to a high gloss.

cn.t: This reimagined production of Lerner and Loewe's 1947 classic earns praise for Alexandra Silber's updated book that modernizes the creaky original while preserving the gorgeous score, brought to life by a Broadway-caliber cast.
